speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; since you are a newborn with a generalized rash, I need to determine if this is infectious, allergic, or systemic. First, tell me how many days old you are and when the rash first appeared. Did it start on your face, trunk, or extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infection is highly unlikely given the 4-day-old age and 1-day rash duration without maternal HSV history; instead, this presentation of a generalized rash starting at day 4 in an infant born to a mother with a history of untreated gonorrhea is most consistent with early disseminated gonococcal infection or a non-specific neonatal exanthem. Given the high suspicion of a bacterial etiology like Neisseria gonorrhoeae or early viral infection despite the timeline, I request a CBC and blood culture. REQUEST TEST: CBC and Blood Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_photos
